### `compute`

```text
Usage: compute [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  MeshForge compute fabric command-line tool.

Options:
  --version             Print the version and exit.
  --token-file <file>   File holding a bearer token to send instead of the `compute login` one
                        (overrides [cli] token and MESHFORGE_CLI__TOKEN). Never pass a token itself
                        on the command line.
  --ca <file>           The fabric CA certificate (ca.crt) to verify the controller with (overrides
                        [cli] ca_file; found automatically on a laptop with an enrolled agent or the
                        controller).
  --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the
                        installation.
  --help                Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  nodes      List the fabric's nodes, or show one node.
  status     Show where the controller is, whether it answers, and what it reports.
  run        Submit a project as a job (and optionally follow it).
  jobs       List recent jobs, newest first (or show one job in detail).
  logs       Print a job's logs (stdout to stdout, stderr to stderr).
  cancel     Cancel a job (idempotent).
  get        Download a finished job's outputs (verified) and unpack them.
  watch      Watch a split job's progress per chunk and per node until it ends (--json: print...
  explain    Why the planner placed (or has not placed) a job: every candidate, rejections with...
  network    The measured network matrix: bandwidth, RTT and age of every probed node pair,...
  login      Log in to the controller and keep an API token for later commands.
  logout     Revoke the stored API token on the controller and forget it here.
  whoami     Who the controller says you are, and until when your login lasts.
  tokens     List or revoke your API tokens (V0.7).
  secret     Store, list or delete your job secrets (V0.7; values never shown).
  data       Named inputs: datasets and models registered once, used by name.
  node       Act on one node (or all of them).
  fabric     Invite laptops into the fabric and join one (V0.7).
  bench      Benchmark workloads and campaigns (V0.9).
  telemetry  Export the telemetry dataset (run records) as Parquet (V0.9; admin).
  planner    The planner's calibration, offline evaluation (V0.14) and ML data (V0.15).
```

### `compute get`

```text
Usage: compute get [OPTIONS] {JOB_ID}

  Download a finished job's outputs (verified) and unpack them.

  Everything happens in a temporary folder next to the destination (same filesystem): download,
  SHA-256 check, unpack. Only when all of that succeeded is an existing destination moved aside and
  the new folder renamed into place - a missing output, a network error or a digest mismatch leaves
  the old folder exactly as it was.

Arguments:
  JOB_ID  [required]

Options:
  --dest <path>  Where to unpack (default ./outputs/<job_id>).
  --force        Replace a non-empty destination.
  --help         Show this message and exit.
```

### `compute login`

```text
Usage: compute login [OPTIONS]

  Log in to the controller and keep an API token for later commands.

Options:
  --controller <str>   Controller REST URL, e.g. https://192.168.1.20:47110 (default: [cli]
                       controller_url).
  --ca <file>          The fabric's ca.crt to verify the controller with.
  --fingerprint <str>  First contact: the CA's full SHA-256 fingerprint (from `meshforge-controller
                       fabric show`); the CA is read from the handshake and kept only if it matches.
  -u, --user <str>     Your user name.
  --password-stdin     Read the password from the first line of stdin (scripts).
  --token-name <str>   A label for this token (e.g. laptop).  [default: compute]
  --help               Show this message and exit.
```

```text
Usage: compute node revoke [OPTIONS] {node_id}

  Revoke a node (V0.7 D138): its certificate is refused on every plane, its live session is cut now

  new identity.

Arguments:
  node_id  The node to revoke (node_...).  [required]

Options:
  --json  Print the answer as one line of JSON with a schema_version (for scripts; see docs/CLI.md).
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

### `compute nodes`

```text
Usage: compute nodes [OPTIONS] [NODE_ID]

  List the fabric's nodes, or show one node.

  Three liveness fields are shown on purpose and can legitimately disagree (D16): STATE is the
  database's view (offline at once after a clean agent stop, suspect after a dropped connection
  until the lease runs out), CONN is whether this controller process holds the node's stream right
  now, and AGE is how stale the newest resource sample is.

Arguments:
  [NODE_ID]  Show this node's detail instead of the list.

Options:
  --json   Print the answer as one line of JSON with a schema_version (for scripts; see
           docs/CLI.md).
  --watch  Re-render every cli.watch_interval_s seconds until Ctrl-C (exits 0). Ignored with --json.
  --help   Show this message and exit.
```

### `compute planner eval`

```text
Usage: compute planner eval [OPTIONS]

  Evaluate benchmark campaigns: every policy's regret vs the oracle (admin).

Options:
  --campaign <str>         A campaign to evaluate (repeat for several).  [required]
  --holdout <str>          Evaluate only this workload family (held out).
  --allow-leak             Debugging: use the live calibration (every verdict 'leaked').
  --md <path>              Also write the report as Markdown to this file.
  --timeout <float range>  Give up waiting after this many seconds (the evaluation keeps running on
                           the controller). Default: the controller's default fold budget plus the
                           replay margin.  [default: 3600.0; x>=1.0]
  --json                   Print the answer as one line of JSON with a schema_version (for scripts;
                           see docs/CLI.md).
  --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

### `compute planner ml classify`

```text
Usage: compute planner ml classify [OPTIONS]

  The 0.15.10 classifier experiment: classify the winning configuration instead of predicting costs,
  scored by the same regret (report only).

Options:
  --campaign <str>               A benchmark campaign (repeatable; admin).
  --examples <file>              Run on this saved examples document (no controller).
  --save-examples <file>         Also write the controller's examples document to this new file.
  -o, --out <directory>          Keep classify.json and classify.md in this directory.
  --timeout <float range>        Stop the training after this many seconds (exit 1).  [default:
                                 1800.0; x>=1.0]
  --fetch-timeout <float range>  Wait this many seconds for the controller's examples (--campaign).
                                 The controller stops its own build at [controller.planner]
                                 ml_classifier_timeout_s (900 s by default, answer 504); raise both
                                 together.  [default: 1800.0; x>=1.0]
  --json                         Print the answer as one line of JSON with a schema_version (for
                                 scripts; see docs/CLI.md).
  --help                         Show this message and exit.
```

### `compute planner ml compare`

```text
Usage: compute planner ml compare [OPTIONS]

  Compare learned models with the calibration per term (offline, no controller): held-out families,
  conformal intervals, OOD.

Options:
  --dataset <file>            A dataset file from `compute planner ml dataset --out FILE` (its
                              FILE.json sidecar is read when present).  [required]
  --terms <str>               Only these terms (a,b,...).
  --algorithms <str>          Only these learned algorithms (ridge, knn, tree, forest, lightgbm,
                              xgboost); the baselines always run.
  --with-family               Ablation: add the family as a feature.
  --ablations                 Also re-run the evaluation without each feature group and report how
                              much each one matters (about 7x the time: raise --timeout).
  --classify-examples <file>  V0.15 (0.15.10): add the classifier experiment's section from this
                              examples document (`compute planner ml classify --save-examples
                              FILE`).
  --min-rows <int range>      Data floor per term (default 200).  [x>=1]
  --min-families <int range>  Family floor per term (default 3).  [x>=1]
  --min-effect <float range>  `better` needs the held-out log-error gain's CI beyond this (default
                              0.02, about 2 %).  [x>=0.0]
  -o, --out <directory>       Keep report.json and report.md in this directory.
  --timeout <float range>     Stop the comparison after this many seconds (exit 1; the child process
                              is killed).  [default: 3600.0; x>=1.0]
  --json                      Print the answer as one line of JSON with a schema_version (for
                              scripts; see docs/CLI.md).
  --help                      Show this message and exit.
```

### `compute run`

```text
Usage: compute run [OPTIONS] [path]

  Submit a project as a job (and optionally follow it).

  Without --node/--local the controller's planner chooses the node (V0.6); when this laptop runs an
  enrolled agent, it is the Local candidate.

Arguments:
  path  The project folder (default: the current folder).  [default: .]

Options:
  --node <str>             Pin the job to this node (Mode 1).
  --local                  Pin the job to this laptop's own agent.
  --policy <str>           Placement policy for an automatic job: random, round_robin, least_loaded,
                           strongest_suitable, resource_score, cache_affinity, cost_model (default:
                           the manifest's, else the controller's).
  --objective <str>        What the cost_model policy optimises (V0.14): min_time, min_network,
                           prefer_local (default: the manifest's, else the controller's).
  --priority <int range>   Queue priority -10..10 (overrides the manifest's).  [-10<=x<=10]
  -f, --follow             Stream the logs; exit with the job's outcome.
  --name <str>             Job name (overrides the manifest).
  --idempotency-key <str>  Re-submit safely: the same key returns the same job.
  --no-progress            With -f on a split: job, stream the logs instead of showing the progress
                           per chunk and node (for scripts).
  --dry-run                Print what would be submitted (for a split: job its items and chunking)
                           without uploading or submitting anything.
  --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-agent hardware score`

```text
Usage: meshforge-agent hardware score [OPTIONS]

  Measure this machine's hardware scores (CPU, memory, GPU) and cache them.

  Local only, like `hardware show`. Uses the cached run when it is still valid for this hardware and
  software (unless --force). Measurements run in a child process at lowered priority within
  [agent.scores] budget_s. A metric that cannot be measured here (no BLAS, no torch, no CUDA) is
  reported as unavailable with its reason - that is a truthful result, exit 0. Exit 7 (BUSY) if
  another scoring run holds the lock.

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --json           Machine-readable output.
  --force          Measure even if a valid cached run exists.
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

```text
  hardware scores, if any.
```

### `meshforge-agent rotate-key`

```text
Usage: meshforge-agent rotate-key [OPTIONS]

  Give this laptop a new key, keeping its node_id (V0.7 G4, D140).

  Stages a new P-256 key; the running agent renews its certificate with it at its next check
  (`[agent.cert] renew_check_interval_s`), or right after the next start, then switches key,
  certificate and session together. The old key keeps working until then.

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --cancel         Drop a staged key that is not in use yet.
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

```text
Commands:
```

```text
  init-config  Write the packaged controller's first settings file (the package's postinst runs...
```

### `meshforge-controller setup init-config`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller setup init-config [OPTIONS]

  Write the packaged controller's first settings file (the package's postinst runs this once). Never
  overwrites an existing file.

Options:
  --path <path>    Settings file to write (only if missing).  [default:
                   /etc/meshforge/controller.toml]
  --address <str>  LAN IPv4 address to listen on (default: detected).
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller setup url`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller setup url [OPTIONS]

  Print the setup page's link (with its one-time token) for a controller that has no fabric yet.
  Open it in a browser ON THIS MACHINE. Exits 5 when the fabric already exists.

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --json           Machine-readable output.
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller token`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller token [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Show or rotate the fabric token that protects job and blob calls (D44).

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  show    Print the fabric token (creating it if this controller has none yet).
  rotate  Replace the fabric token and print the new one; the old one stops working.
```

### `meshforge-controller token rotate`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller token rotate [OPTIONS]

  Replace the fabric token and print the new one; the old one stops working.

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller token show`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller token show [OPTIONS]

  Print the fabric token (creating it if this controller has none yet).

  Give it to each laptop that submits jobs: `[cli] token` in its config.toml, MESHFORGE_CLI__TOKEN,
  or a file passed with `compute --token-file`.

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller user`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller user [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Manage REST users (V0.7): create, list, disable, enable, reset-password.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  create          Create a REST user (`compute login` signs in as it).
  list            Every user (never a password or a token).
  disable         Disable a user: their API tokens stop working on the next request.
  enable          Enable a disabled user (old tokens stay revoked; they log in again).
  reset-password  Set a new password; every API token of the user is revoked with it.
```

### `meshforge-controller user create`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller user create [OPTIONS] {name}

  Create a REST user (`compute login` signs in as it).

Arguments:
  name  Login name (lower-case a-z 0-9 . _ -).  [required]

Options:
  --admin           An admin: invites, node revoke, every user's jobs.
  --password-stdin  Read the password from the first line of stdin instead of prompting (for
                    scripts; never pass a password as an argument).
  --config <file>   TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --help            Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller user disable`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller user disable [OPTIONS] {name}

  Disable a user: their API tokens stop working on the next request.

Arguments:
  name  The user to disable.  [required]

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller user enable`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller user enable [OPTIONS] {name}

  Enable a disabled user (old tokens stay revoked; they log in again).

Arguments:
  name  The user to enable.  [required]

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller user list`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller user list [OPTIONS]

  Every user (never a password or a token).

Options:
  --config <file>  TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --json           Machine-readable output.
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `meshforge-controller user reset-password`

```text
Usage: meshforge-controller user reset-password [OPTIONS] {name}

  Set a new password; every API token of the user is revoked with it.

Arguments:
  name  The user whose password to set.  [required]

Options:
  --password-stdin  Read the password from the first line of stdin instead of prompting (for
                    scripts; never pass a password as an argument).
  --config <file>   TOML settings file (default: $MESHFORGE_CONFIG or <config dir>/config.toml).
  --help            Show this message and exit.
```
